as_told.title: Corso had 24 hours to edit The Day After Roswell

plain: The Day After Roswell was hurried out with almost no time to edit it, and its author was upset by the result, or so the people who tell this story say. The book was published in 1997 by Philip J. Corso, a retired Army officer. In it he wrote about Roswell, the New Mexico town at the centre of a famous 1947 claim that a flying saucer crashed there. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells Michels what he was told: the book was "rushed to print" with Corso's co-writer, William J. Birnes. Fox also names a man called Michael Hessman as part of the story. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb tells it a little differently, as a rumour. In his version Corso had only 24 hours to edit the book, and according to Corso's son he "put his hand to his head and said, 'I can't believe this.'" Both men are passing on what others told them. If it is true, some of the book's mistakes could come from the rush rather than from Corso himself.
